Audi's sweeping turn signals, also called dynamic LED indicators, have become a signature feature across all their models. Both the US and EU regulate sequential turn signals using standards that trace back to UN Regulation 48, requiring the sweep to move outward toward the signalled direction. The US went a step further in its 2021 update to SAE J588, incorporated into federal standard FMVSS 108. This forced Audi to alter their dynamic turn signal pattern for US market cars, a difference that is still visible today between US and EU versions — one of those things where once you see it, you cannot unsee it. Audi initially could not offer the signals on US cars at all, later resorting to hardware changes including separate bumper-mounted reflectors alongside software adjustments to reach compliance. What US regulatory requirement forced Audi to modify its iconic sequential turn signals?
Looking for a general funda, not the exact rule.
